key_insight: Microroller speed drops as confinement increases, and in sufficiently narrow channels the motion can reverse direction because far-field rotlet stresses and near-field shear resistance compete.
engineering_relevance: The scaling framework provides a geometry-aware way to predict and control microroller transport in microfluidic and biomedical devices under confined flow conditions.
method: Experiments in constricted, rectangular, and cylindrical microchannels
Numerical simulations of microroller translation under varying confinement
Scaling analysis using a force-free translation condition across geometries
evidence_signal: The proposed scaling laws for translational velocity match the experimental and simulation results across multiple channel geometries and confinement levels.
watch_item: The velocity reversal depends strongly on channel geometry and tight confinement, so designs may need geometry-specific calibration rather than a single universal threshold.
paper_title: Dynamics of a microroller under confinement
